steps.text: Preheat an oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Beat the butter and sugar with an electric mixer in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Add the egg and the vanilla and beat until well combined. Stir in the mashed banana, set aside.
Stir together the flour, baking soda, baking powder, and salt in a separate large bowl, and make a well in the center. Pour the banana mixture into the well and stir just until combined.

Remove half of the batter from the bowl. Mix the cocoa powder into the batter remaining in the bowl and stir well. Spread the cocoa batter in the bottom of the prepared pan. Spoon the remaining batter on top and use a knife to swirl the batter into a marbled design.
Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are golden, about 25 minutes. Allow to cool before cutting into 24 pieces.

raw_recipe.headline: Cocoa Banana Bars
raw_recipe.description: These pretty, marbled bar cookies are very moist with a rich banana and chocolate flavor.

review.reviewBody: I make these all the time for Potluck...the only bad thing about them is keeping DH from devouring them all before-hand! I usually put the chocolate layer on top so I only have to use one bowl. I also sometimes add walnuts and/or chocolate chips. Yummy!

This recipe makes a delicious chocolate flavored banana cake. If you are expecting a bar cookie, or chewy brownie type..this recipe won't cut it. That being said, these are very good. I was a little worried about dryness as mentioned by several others so I used almost a full 2 cups of banana...perfect...very moist and the banana flavor comes through nicely. I though they could use a little something on the top. I made a peanut butter glaze (from this site) as suggested by another reviewer and just drizzled that over the top. With that addition, this recipe was 5 stars! Perhaps just a sifting of confectioner's sugar would be enough, but how can one go wrong with banana, chocolate and peanut butter all in one bite!

I added 3T mayo to the cocoa portion, decreased the sugar to 2/3 C, added chocolate chips to the top portion, and sprinkled generously with cinnamon/sugar mixture before baking (I add this step to every banana bread recipe I try....it is delicious). These are a great alternative to banana bread. This recipe is also listed on Taste of Home's website under Black Bottom Banana Bars and a reviewer mentioned the 3T of mayo...definitely ups the moisture. I also baked it in an 11 x 7 pan for approx 40 minutes.

Yummy, very moist. If you don't have enough bananas you can substitute with applesauce if you've got it on hand. When dividing the mix you'll be removing about 2.5 cups as the total mixture is about 5 cups (although I used just under of 2 cups of banana/applesauce mix to get this amount). The texture of it is not like a typical "Bar" it's more like a moist cake, so baking it in a loaf pan, cake pan or muffin pan is a great idea. You could ice it as well & I'm sure that would be tasty - I think chocolate or cream cheese icing would be good for this recipe. Thank you Lisa for this recipe, it's a "Do Over" for me.

Baked for 20 min til brown on edges.

Add splash of coffee to chocolate batter and extra cocoa.

Used four large black bananas.

I too, thought it looked thin in a 9x13 pan, but it came out perfectly. Very glad I didn't try a smaller pan. I did alter the recipe a bit because I am such a chocoholic. I added 1 cup of chocolate chips before dividing the batter to add the cocoa. I also topped the cake with confectioners sugar after it cooled. So good!

Not gonna let ripe bananas go to waste around here if I can bake them! These were a big hit! Agree that the batter was a little dry so I added a splash of vanilla almond milk. Also, made with King Arthur gluten free measure for measure flour and texture came out soft and smooth. 3 small super ripe bananas used. Not too sweet, definitely a keeper!!

Recipe is great but I use an 11 x 7 pan to bake. If I double the batch I will use a 13 x 9 pan. We like it 'cake like' and the only way to achieve that is by doing the above. I also use gluten free flour and it still comes out fantastic!

I made this as cupcakes. I used an ice cream scoop and scooped half in chocolate and half in the traditional batter. The topping was sprinkle of chocolate chips which I pushed down into the batter with a knife. Everybody loved them!
I don't even like banana cake---- but I couldn't stop eating this! I added about 1/4 cup more banana and used almond extract instead of vanilla. I also added a sugar glaze to the top. AMAZING!

Subbed caramel extract for vanilla to liven the flavor up, but these were still somewhat bland (like a cake without icing). Batter was thick & thus didn't "marbleize" very easily....was hoping the appearance would make up for the lack of flavor. Would recommend drizzling with caramel sauce or adding chocolate chips to chocolate layer. Probably better to get rid of your bananas by making muffins or bread...
UPDATE: Made a caramel sauce & drizzled over top. This modification added a touch of sweetness/flavor & visual interest that made it worthy of 4 stars (in my humble opinion).
I’ve already made this twice since finding it the other day! We love it! My oldest grandson asked for it for breakfast! It’s more cake like so we now call it chocolate banana cake!
In the oven as we speak!

Because of food allergies, I replaced the butter with Olive oil, the egg with flax meal, and the flour with gluten free flour. And To avoid all the sugar, I replaced half with truvia (the kind good for baking). And it came out WONDERFUL. A healthier version too. I’m thrilled. 😎

These were excellent! I used four over-ripe medium-sized bananas which amounted to slightly more than 1.5 cups, but it was fine. They are thin, like brownies, but more like a cake than a denser brownie consistency. Mine needed 35 minutes to bake but that might just be my oven. I may toss in some nuts next time.
I’ve had more praise for this cake than anything I’ve made before. Months after I brought it into the office, people are still talking about it.

I made these as cupcakes but kept the recipe as is. I used 4 ripe bananas - put in my ninja it showed 2 cups pureed banana. Plan to ice them (regular white icing - although I may try peanut butter icing like another review said) and take them to a meeting dinner - my husband said they were really good.
Gluten-free version with cup-for-cup flour was excellent! Great texture, and everyone devoured them!

It was delicious! Followed the recipe exactly and was so pleasantly surprised to get a moist, airy cake instead of dense bars! Will definitely have to make it again, my cat ate it while I was sleeping so I’ll be making another one today.
Made a double batch: first 12 muffins without cocoa and the next 12 muffins with the cocoa plus chocolate chips. They took 20 minutes to cook and turned out well.
